title: NY Fed SCE: expected chance of moving home, ten-cell demographic profile
brief: Revision 2 records the owner's decisions: the doc's ten cells (3 age, 3 income, 4 region) and no national round, with the national mean shown only. Resolution is 'the first archived workbook carrying month M'. Each month, entrants forecast the mean percent chance that US household heads expect to move to a different primary residence in the next 12 months, and the ten cells are scored together as one profile. The source is the NY Fed SCE workbook the arena already archives every day. The zero point is per-cell persistence with a measured spread, which equals the default 1.5. There is no unscored pilot, because the card measured late fill-in directly: 74 daily captures with no revised value. First scored lock: Sat 2026-12-05 11:00 ET (November survey, released Mon 2026-12-07). For maintainers: the rights verdict is proposed as approved, the same file and licence as the integrated SCE source. Also see the separate note sce-capture-bug.md: the capture dated release day is taken before the release.
question: NY Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations, survey month M: for each of ten demographic cells (age under 40, 40-60, over 60; income under $50k, $50-100k, over $100k; region West, Midwest, South, Northeast), what will be the mean reported percent chance that a household head will move to a different primary residence over the next 12 months?

source.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Center for Microeconomic Data, Survey of Consumer Expectations (SCE). A monthly rotating internet panel of about 1,300 US household heads [owner doc; consistent with docs/sources/ny-fed-sce.md on origin/dev].
source.access: The all-history workbook https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/interactives/sce/sce/downloads/data/frbny-sce-data.xlsx, which the arena already fetches and archives write-once per UTC day under sources/sce/<YYYY-MM-DD>.xlsx (ssa/adapters/sce.py on origin/dev; 74 captures from 2026-08-26 to 2026-11-08). No key and no account. New work is a reader for two more sheets in the same file, located by sheet name and exact header string, never by position: 'Moving expectations' (column header 'Mean probability of changing primary residence over the next 12 months') and 'Moving expectations Demo' (headers 'Age Under 40', 'Age 40-60', 'Age Over 60', 'Income under 50k', 'Income 50-100k', 'Income Over 100k', 'Region West', 'Region Midwest', 'Region South', 'Region Northeast'). Rows are YYYYMM integers in column A, from 201306 [verified on the 2026-11-08 capture: 160 rows, 201306 to 202609]. Fetch check: one GET with an honest, non-browser user agent at 2026-11-09T01:06:27Z returned HTTP 200, 1,100,751 bytes, sha256 6512ecde..., identical to the 2026-11-08 archive [verified]. The adapter's docstring says the NY Fed 403s generic clients, so it sends a desktop-browser user agent. That was not reproduced from this sandbox (see process notes); maintainers may want to retest it from a runner.
source.archive_policy: Use: allowed. Redistribution of the archived workbook and derived numbers: allowed. Automated retrieval: already approved for this exact file (ssa/inventory.py 'sce': rights APPROVED, state INTEGRATED). Evidence: the workbook's own 'License' sheet, read from the 2026-11-08 capture [verified]: 'FRBNY grants users, who may be individuals or entities, a worldwide, royalty-free, nonexclusive right to reproduce, use, and distribute the SCE questions and FRBNY-published SCE data, in whole or in part, and to produce, reproduce, and distribute work derived from or based on the SCE questions and the FRBNY-published SCE data.' Conditions: no FRBNY logo or trademark; no implied endorsement; any publication or presentation of SCE data carries the required attribution: 'Source: Survey of Consumer Expectations, © 2013-2026 Federal Reserve Bank of New York (FRBNY). The SCE data are available without charge at http://www.newyorkfed.org/microeconomics/sce and may be used subject to license terms posted there. FRBNY disclaims any responsibility for this analysis and interpretation of Survey of Consumer Expectations data.' The licence does not address automated retrieval in words. The owner doc says the NY Fed terms allow distribution 'including by automated means'. That could not be checked: https://www.newyorkfed.org/terms-of-use returned 302 to /errors/404 at 2026-11-09T01:06:05Z. Proposed verdict: approved, on the same basis as the integrated SCE source. Maintainers decide. Task for a person (G4), not blocking: open https://www.newyorkfed.org/microeconomics/sce in a browser, follow its terms or legal link, and paste the sentence on automated access into the PR. The URL tried here (/terms-of-use) is a 404. No message to the NY Fed is needed.

target.population: US household heads in the SCE panel (about 1,300 a month), all respondents to the moving question, which the owner doc gives as Q3: 'what do you think is the percent chance that over the next 12 months you will move to a different primary residence'. The published statistic is the mean probability across respondents in each cell, as the NY Fed weights and publishes it. This is a stated intention, not an observed move: the panel's follow-up D3 (did a repeat respondent actually move) is not published as a series [owner doc, unverified]. Ten cells, frozen at season start: age (3), income (3), region (4). Education (3) and numeracy (2) are left out, per the owner doc.
target.window: Survey month M, as labelled in column A of the workbook (YYYYMM). Fielding happens during M. The release lands early in M+1 at 11:00 ET, on a date the NY Fed preannounces for the calendar year.
target.calculation: For each cell, the value in row M of 'Moving expectations Demo', in the column whose header string is exactly the cell name, read from the resolution vintage at full stored precision (the workbook stores float32, e.g. 25.86676597595215). No rounding before scoring. The national mean is read from the 'Moving expectations' sheet and is shown, not scored (owner decision, rev 2).
target.unit: Percent chance (0-100), mean across respondents in the cell

lock: No unscored pilot (owner decision G3 exemption): the card measured late fill-in directly. In 74 daily captures from 2026-08-26 to 2026-11-08, no published value changed, and the reader extends an adapter already in live use. Release minus 48 hours, the arena's rule for SCE rounds: 11:00 America/New_York two days before the release date on the NY Fed calendar. First scored lock: Sat 2026-12-05 11:00 ET (16:00Z), for the November 2026 survey; release Mon 2026-12-07 11:00 ET (dates as in SCE_RELEASES in tools/generate_rounds.py on origin/dev, which the maintainers copied from the NY Fed calendar). The existing November SCE inflation rounds store lock_at 2026-12-05T15:00:00Z and release_at 2026-12-07T15:00:00Z, which is 10:00 EST: an hour early, because US daylight time ended on 2026-11-01. This card uses 16:00Z (11:00 EST), and maintainers should align the two (see sce-capture-bug.md). Timing (lesson 7): the change needs about two weeks to reach main, so main is reached about 2026-11-22 to 11-24. That leaves participants 11 to 13 days before the 12-05 lock. If main is reached after 2026-11-28, the first scored lock moves to the December 2026 survey, released in early January 2027. Its date needs the NY Fed's 2027 calendar, which is not yet in SCE_RELEASES. The October 2026 survey (released Mon 2026-11-09) locked on 2026-11-07 and cannot be used. At lock, the newest published month is M-1: September 2026 data was the newest in every capture from 2026-10-08 to 2026-11-08 [verified].
baseline: Ranked zero point: per-cell persistence, meaning each cell's value for month M-1 from the newest vintage archived before the lock. In the general family it is mean_k with k = 1 and an rms_n spread (owner decision G1). Spread: measured, equals the default. The RMS of persistence's own errors over the 12 previous months (rms_12) scores within 0.3% of sd 1.5, so the round keeps the arena's per-cell sd 1.5 (ssa/profile_round.persistence_profile via baselines.persistence, owner decision G2) and no new code is needed. Lesson 12 check [verified computation, 2026-11-08 capture, 36 target months 2023-10 to 2026-09, arena scoring.energy_score with its fixed 400-point design]: persistence with sd 1.5 has mean energy score 3.309. Persistence with an honest per-cell sd (RMS of its own error over the 12 previous months) has 3.318, so an entrant gains -0.3% by submitting the reference with an honest spread. sd 1.5 is already close to honest here, because cell errors run 0.8 to 1.7 points. Also shown, not ranked: the 6-month mean per cell, with an RMS-12 spread. It is worse than persistence (energy score 3.578, -7.8%), so persistence is the stronger simple reference. Per-cell numbers over the same 36 months [verified; they match the owner doc's table within 0.02], given as persistence MAE / 6-month-mean MAE / noise m / real movement s (arena scoring.noise_floor): under 40 1.65/1.34/1.44/0.00 (noise only); 40-60 0.86/1.19/0.40/0.97; over 60 0.81/0.89/0.42/0.87; under 50k 1.31/1.20/0.52/1.32; 50-100k 1.28/1.07/1.01/0.54; over 100k 0.94/1.38/0.00/1.18; West 1.23/1.76/0.00/1.54; Midwest 1.55/1.43/0.99/1.25; South 1.00/1.22/0.40/1.13; Northeast 1.51/1.60/1.12/0.88. National 0.72/0.86/0.33/0.74.
resolution: The first archived workbook carrying month M (owner decision, rev 2): the first vintage under sources/sce/, by capture day, whose newest reference month is M and whose capture is at or after release_at. Each cell resolves on its row-M value in that vintage. This differs from the wording of the existing SCE rounds ('the vintage archived ... on release day'). The arena's daily capture runs at about 04:30 to 06:10 UTC, before the 11:00 ET release, and is write-once per day. So the file dated release day holds the previous month: sources/sce/2026-09-08.xlsx has newest month 2026-07 and the same sha256 (503a7787...) as 2026-08-26. The first file with August is 2026-09-09; for September, 2026-10-07 holds August and 2026-10-08 holds September [verified, all 74 captures]. The existing rounds resolved correctly anyway, from a live in-memory fetch at 2026-09-08T16:52Z ('first point in the series after the pre-lock history', resolutions/resolved.json). But the bytes they resolved on were not archived that day. Revisions: in all 74 captures, every already-published month's value in all 15 demo columns is identical (max absolute difference 0) [verified]. So the next-day vintage carries the release-day numbers. The capture timing is written up for maintainers in sce-capture-bug.md (housing folder), because it also affects the live sce-2026-11-* rounds.
missing_data_policy: (1) Release postponed: if the NY Fed moves the date before the lock, the lock moves with it to the new release minus 48h. If the move is announced after the lock, forecasts stand and the round resolves on the delayed release. (2) No vintage carrying month M by release + 7 days: the round is cancelled, never resolved from a later month. (3) A cell's row-M value missing, non-numeric or outside 0-100, or a header not found exactly: the reader raises and the round does not resolve until a maintainer looks. A partial profile is never scored. If not fixed by release + 7 days, the round is cancelled. (4) Lock reference: if the newest vintage before the lock does not carry month M-1, the round refuses to post its reference (lesson 13). A revised past value (none seen so far) never changes a resolved round.
scoring: Arena profile scoring: entrants submit ten cells, each as {mean, sd} with sd > 0 or a quantile map including 0.5. Cells are scored jointly with the energy score (scoring.energy_score, deterministic 400-point design, seed 20260811), and reported as level plus structure (scoring.profile_scores), as on the YouGov and Civiqs profile tasks. Skill = 1 - ES(entrant) / ES(per-cell persistence). Each cell's noise floor is printed in the question text, as yougov_xtab does. Persona condition: possible, since the instrument is public. The arena's persona population table has party, age and education margins but not income or region (owner doc open item), so the persona arm can run the age cells only until that table is extended.

assumptions: Owner decisions, wave 2 (Claude, delegated by Haoyang Shang, 2026-11-08; file DECISIONS-wave2.md). Cells A: the doc's ten (age 3, income 3, region 4); runner-up B, eight cells without the two noise-only cells. National A: shown, not a separate round; runner-up B, a scalar round, which would have needed an rms_12-spread zero point (+7% free against sd 1.5). Resolution: 'first archived workbook carrying month M'.

Resolution reads the first vintage that carries month M, not the vintage dated release day. Reason: the archive shows the release-day capture predates the release (Resolution), and the values are never revised. So the next-day capture carries the release-day numbers, and it is the earliest archived file that can be checked later. Runner-up: add a post-release capture on release day (e.g. a second capture after 15:30Z). That changes the adapter's write-once-per-day rule, so it is a maintainer decision, not this card's.

Zero point kept as the arena default (per-cell persistence, sd 1.5), with no new reference. Reason: measured, it is within 0.3% of an honest spread (lesson 12 check), and the 6-month mean is worse. Runner-up: per-cell RMS-12 spread, which is no better here and needs code.

Cancellation window of release + 7 days, chosen by the agent. Reason: the next capture after a release has always been the next day, and the capture runs daily. Runner-up: release + 3 days. Easy to change.

Suggested arena names, for implementation: tracker 'ny_fed_sce' (existing); series 'sce_moving_<cell>' with a profile cell list; round_id 'sce-<YYYY-MM>-moving'. The reader extends ssa/adapters/sce.py with a second sheet and header map, and keeps the existing inflation reader byte-identical. Naming changes no rule.
